title: ADR captures a single decision and rationale
claim: An ADR captures a single architectural decision and its rationale, while a collection of ADRs forms a decision log.
evidence: ADR site describes ADRs as capturing one justified design choice and the collection as a decision log.
relevance: The feature should generate standalone decision records, not plans or implementation transcripts.

title: Classic ADR sections are title status context decision consequences
claim: Nygard-style ADRs use a compact structure with title, status, context, decision, and consequences.
evidence: ADR Templates page summarizes Nygard ADR structure.
relevance: Cartographer ADR output should keep the record compact and durable.

title: ADR logs should be append-only with superseding links
claim: Accepted ADRs should not be rewritten when direction changes; a new record should supersede the original and link the two together.
evidence: Microsoft ADR guidance says the log serves as an append-only log and changed decisions should be recorded by a new superseding record.
relevance: Cartographer should use graph edges for supersession/currentness rather than mutating old ADR bodies.

title: Useful ADR metadata includes status tradeoffs and confidence
claim: ADR records should include status, options/tradeoffs, decision outcome, and confidence where useful.
evidence: Microsoft ADR guidance lists problem/context, options considered, decision outcome, tradeoffs, confidence, and status.
relevance: Searchable metadata and durable summaries should be first-class in generated ADRs.

title: Numbered ADR filenames are a common convention
claim: Common ADR guidance uses ascending numbers in filenames or titles, with date and status metadata; MADR suggests copying templates into docs/decisions/nnnn-title.md.
evidence: Microsoft playbook describes ascending numbers and dates/status; MADR README suggests docs/decisions/nnnn-title.md.
relevance: Cartographer should choose a chronological filename scheme that is easy to sort and query.

title: ADRs should be pithy standalone records
claim: ADR guidance emphasizes records that are pithy, factual, on-topic, and stand alone without being design guides.
evidence: Microsoft ADR guidance warns against making ADRs design guides and says decisions must be clear and stand alone.
relevance: Generated ADRs should avoid brittle line-level references and lengthy proposal/plan detail.

title: Current Cartographer explicitly treats ADR generation as future work
claim: Current Cartographer workflow docs state final concise ADR generation into docs is out of scope and belongs to a later proposal.
evidence: README and workflow skills include explicit non-goal/future-work notes about ADR generation outside .plan.
relevance: This proposal fills a known workflow gap rather than changing accepted plan/proposal behavior unexpectedly.

title: Cartographer already has durable validation receipts and context packs
claim: Cartographer workflow artifacts now include receipts and context packs that summarize implementation validation and phase context outside the chat transcript.
evidence: README documents receipts/context-packs and workflow-optimization artifacts include these records.
relevance: ADR generation can consume validated receipts/context packs instead of raw chat or stale plan prose.

title: Cartographer validators can be extended to validate ADR graphs
claim: Cartographer already has JSONL validators and planning graph validators for map/fact/plan/receipt artifacts.
evidence: Current manage_jsonl.ts and validate_planning_graph.py validate JSONL records, lifecycle metadata, references, and workflow state.
relevance: ADR node/edge graph validation can reuse existing JSONL validation patterns.

title: User ADR feature open-question answers
description: User answered ADR proposal open questions about directory discovery, adr_required proposal gating, option evaluation prompts, and legacy ADR imports.

title: ADR directory should prefer existing conventions
claim: The ADR generator should search for an existing ADR or decisions folder and use it; if none exists, it should default to docs/adr.
evidence: User explicitly answered open question 1 with this directory-selection preference.
relevance: The proposal should avoid forcing docs/adr when a repository already has an ADR/decisions convention.

title: ADR generation should be proposal-gated
claim: ADR generation should happen only when the proposal marks adr_required true, and the proposal summary should tell the user whether an ADR will be generated so they can change it before planning and implementation begin.
evidence: User explicitly answered open question 2 with proposal-time adr_required gating and user-visible summary behavior.
relevance: The proposal workflow must record ADR intent before plan/implementation rather than deciding only at finalization.

title: ADR-worthy dictated choices need alternatives or rationale
claim: When the proposal generator detects an architectural decision such as adding Auth0 but no options were considered, it should prompt the user to either evaluate alternatives or provide the reason for the chosen option.
evidence: User gave Auth0 as an example and stated ADRs require other options considered unless the user provides the decision rationale.
relevance: Generated ADRs require a considered-options section and should not invent rationale for user-directed choices.

title: Legacy ADR imports may omit validation receipts
claim: Imported legacy ADRs should be allowed without validation receipts when they pass schema validation and are explicitly marked as legacy.
evidence: User answered yes to allowing imported legacy ADRs without validation receipts if marked accepted-legacy or similar.
relevance: ADR validation needs a separate legacy import path from normal accepted generated ADRs.

title: User ADR standalone tool decision
description: User clarified that ADR creation, lookup, and management should always be available outside the full Cartographer workflow, and agreed to a dedicated cartographer_adr tool model.

title: ADR management should use a dedicated tool
claim: ADR creation, lookup, and management should be exposed through a dedicated user-facing cartographer_adr tool, while cartographer_jsonl remains a low-level utility ADR tooling can reuse internally.
evidence: User agreed that standalone ADR work fits the new dedicated tool model better than adding domain behavior to cartographer_jsonl.
relevance: The proposal should make ADRs a general repository capability rather than a feature hidden behind proposal/plan/implement workflows.
